overview: Shu Han claimed legitimacy as the true successor to the Han dynasty, ruling Sichuan under Liu Bei and his famous chancellor Zhuge Liang. Though the smallest of the Three Kingdoms, it became the most romanticized in later literature.

items.text: The repeating crossbow, known since the Warring States, was improved under Zhuge Liang by tradition, along with the wooden ox, a wheelbarrow-like cart for carrying supplies over mountain roads.
Sichuan's irrigation, built around the Dujiangyan works of the third century BCE, was kept up and extended to feed the state.
Confucian legitimacy theory justified resistance to Cao Wei.
Loyalty and righteousness became central virtues in Shu Han ideology.
Zhuge Liang became the archetype of the brilliant but tragic loyal minister in Chinese culture.

fall.text: Cao Wei general Deng Ai led a surprise attack through mountain passes and captured Chengdu, forcing Liu Shan to surrender.
